00764| function getStatusIcon(
00765| 	status: string | undefined,
00766| 	toolName?: string,
00767| 	input?: Record<string, unknown>,
00768| ) {
00769| 	// For running/pending, show spinner or clock
00770| 	if (status === "pending") {
00771| 		return <Clock className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-muted-foreground" />;
00772| 	}
00773| 	if (status === "running") {
00774| 		return <Loader2 className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-primary animate-spin" />;
00775| 	}
00776| 	if (status === "error") {
00777| 		return <XCircle className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-red-500 dark:text-red-400" />;
00778| 	}
00779| 
00780| 	// For completed or unknown status, show tool-specific icon
00781| 	if (toolName) {
00782| 		return getToolIcon(toolName, input);
00783| 	}
00784| 
00785| 	if (status === "completed") {
00786| 		return <CheckCircle2 className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-primary" />;
00787| 	}
00788| 
00789| 	return <Wrench className="w-3.5 h-3.5 text-muted-foreground" />;
00790| }
00791| 
00792| function getStatusClasses(status: string | undefined) {
00793| 	switch (status) {
00794| 		case "pending":
00795| 			return "border-border bg-card";
00796| 		case "running":
00797| 			return "border-primary/30 bg-primary/5";
00798| 		case "completed":
00799| 			return "border-border bg-card";
00800| 		case "error":
00801| 			return "border-red-500/30 dark:border-red-900/50 bg-red-500/5 dark:bg-red-950/20";
00802| 		default:
00803| 			return "border-border bg-card";
00804| 	}
00805| }
00806| 
00807| function formatDuration(
00808| 	start: number | undefined,
00809| 	end: number | undefined,
00810| ): string {
00811| 	if (!start) return "";
00812| 	const endTime = end || Date.now();
00813| 	const duration = endTime - start;
00814| 	if (duration < 1000) return `${duration}ms`;
00815| 	if (duration < 60000) return `${(duration / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`;
00816| 	return `${Math.floor(duration / 60000)}m ${((duration % 60000) / 1000).toFixed(0)}s`;
00817| }
00818| 
00819| export function ToolCallCard({
00820| 	part,
00821| 	defaultCollapsed = true,
00822| 	hideTodoTools = false,
00823| }: ToolCallCardProps) {
00824| 	const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(!defaultCollapsed);
00825| 	const { tool, state } = part;
00826| 
00827| 	const toolName = tool || "Unknown Tool";
00828| 	const status = state?.status;
00829| 	const title = state?.title || toolName;
00830| 	const input = state?.input;
00831| 	const output = state?.output;
00832| 	const duration = formatDuration(state?.time?.start, state?.time?.end);
00833| 
00834| 	// Hide todo tools if requested (they're shown in sidebar instead)
00835| 	if (hideTodoTools && toolName.toLowerCase().includes("todo")) {
00836| 		return null;
00837| 	}
00838| 
00839| 	const hasContent = input || output;
00840| 
00841| 	return (
00842| 		<div
00843| 			className={cn(
00844| 				"rounded-lg border transition-all duration-200",
00845| 				getStatusClasses(status),
00846| 			)}
00847| 		>
00848| 			<button
00849| 				type="button"
00850| 				onClick={() => hasContent && setIsOpen(!isOpen)}
00851| 				disabled={!hasContent}
00852| 				className={cn(
00853| 					"w-full flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-2 text-left",
00854| 					hasContent && "cursor-pointer hover:bg-muted/50",
00855| 					!hasContent && "cursor-default",
00856| 				)}
00857| 			>
00858| 				{hasContent && (
00859| 					<ChevronRight
00860| 						className={cn(
00861| 							"w-4 h-4 text-muted-foreground transition-transform duration-200 flex-shrink-0",
00862| 							isOpen && "rotate-90",
00863| 						)}
00864| 					/>
00865| 				)}
00866| 				{!hasContent && <div className="w-4" />}
00867| 
00868| 				{getStatusIcon(status, toolName, input)}
00869| 
00870| 				<span className="flex-1 text-sm font-medium text-foreground truncate">
00871| 					{title}
00872| 				</span>
00873| 
00874| 				{duration && (
00875| 					<span className="text-xs text-foreground/60 dark:text-muted-foreground flex-shrink-0">
00876| 						{duration}
00877| 					</span>
00878| 				)}
00879| 			</button>
00880| 
00881| 			{isOpen && hasContent && (
00882| 				<div className="px-3 pb-3 space-y-2 border-t border-border pt-2">
00883| 					{input && Object.keys(input).length > 0 && (
00884| 						<div>
00885| 							{/* Render input based on tool type */}
00886| 							{isTodoList(input) ? (
00887| 								<>
00888| 									<div className="flex items-center justify-between mb-1">
00889| 										<span className="text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-foreground/60 dark:text-muted-foreground">
00890| 											Todo List

00892| 										<CopyButton text={JSON.stringify(input, null, 2)} />
00893| 									</div>
00894| 									<div
00895| 										className="rounded-md p-2 max-h-64 overflow-y-auto"
00896| 										style={{ backgroundColor: "var(--code-bg)" }}
00897| 									>

00899| 									</div>
00900| 								</>
00901| 							) : isTaskCall(input) ? (

02884| const MessageGroupCard = memo(function MessageGroupCard({
02885| 	group,
02886| 	persona,
02887| }: { group: MessageGroup; persona?: Persona | null }) {
02888| 	const isUser = group.role === "user";
02889| 
02890| 	// Get created time from first message
02891| 	const firstMessage = group.messages[0];
02892| 	const createdAt = firstMessage.info.time?.created
02893| 		? new Date(firstMessage.info.time.created)
02894| 		: null;
02895| 
02896| 	// Get all parts from all messages in order, preserving their sequence
02897| 	const allParts = group.messages.flatMap((msg) => msg.parts);
02898| 
02899| 	// Group consecutive text parts together, but keep tool and other parts separate
02900| 	// This creates "segments" that maintain the original order
02901| 	type Segment =
02902| 		| { key: string; type: "text"; content: string }
02903| 		| { key: string; type: "tool"; part: OpenCodePart }
02904| 		| { key: string; type: "other"; part: OpenCodePart };
02905| 
02906| 	const segments: Segment[] = [];
02907| 	let currentTextBuffer: string[] = [];
02908| 	let currentTextKeys: string[] = [];
02909| 
02910| 	const flushTextBuffer = () => {
02911| 		if (currentTextBuffer.length > 0) {
02912| 			const key = currentTextKeys[0] ?? `text-${segments.length}`;
02913| 			segments.push({
02914| 				key,
02915| 				type: "text",
02916| 				content: currentTextBuffer.join("\n\n"),
02917| 			});
02918| 			currentTextBuffer = [];
02919| 			currentTextKeys = [];
02920| 		}
02921| 	};
02922| 
02923| 	for (const [index, part] of allParts.entries()) {
02924| 		const partKey = part.id ?? `${part.type}-${index}`;
02925| 		if (part.type === "text" && typeof part.text === "string") {
02926| 			currentTextBuffer.push(part.text);
02927| 			currentTextKeys.push(partKey);
02928| 		} else if (part.type === "tool") {
02929| 			flushTextBuffer();
02930| 			segments.push({ key: partKey, type: "tool", part });
02931| 		} else {
02932| 			flushTextBuffer();
02933| 			segments.push({ key: partKey, type: "other", part });
02934| 		}
02935| 	}
02936| 	flushTextBuffer();
02937| 
02938| 	// Get all text content for copy button
02939| 	const allTextContent = allParts
02940| 		.filter(
02941| 			(p): p is OpenCodePart & { type: "text"; text: string } =>
02942| 				p.type === "text" && typeof p.text === "string",
02943| 		)
02944| 		.map((p) => p.text)
02945| 		.join("\n\n");
02946| 
02947| 	// Get assistant display name from persona or default to "Assistant"
02948| 	const assistantName = persona?.name || "Assistant";
02949| 	const personaColor = persona?.color;
02950| 
02951| 	return (
02952| 		<div
02953| 			className={cn(
02954| 				"transition-all duration-200 overflow-hidden",
02955| 				isUser
02956| 					? "sm:ml-8 bg-primary/20 dark:bg-primary/10 border border-primary/40 dark:border-primary/30"
02957| 					: "sm:mr-8 bg-muted/50 border border-border",
02958| 			)}
02959| 			style={
02960| 				!isUser && personaColor
02961| 					? { borderLeftColor: personaColor, borderLeftWidth: "3px" }
02962| 					: undefined
02963| 			}
02964| 		>
02965| 			{/* Header */}
02966| 			<div
02967| 				className={cn(
02968| 					"compact-header flex items-center gap-1 sm:gap-2 px-2 sm:px-3 py-1.5 sm:py-2 border-b",
02969| 					isUser ? "border-primary/30 dark:border-primary/20" : "border-border",
02970| 				)}
02971| 			>
02972| 				{isUser ? (
02973| 					<User className="w-3 h-3 sm:w-4 sm:h-4 text-primary flex-shrink-0" />
02974| 				) : personaColor ? (
02975| 					<div
02976| 						className="w-3 h-3 sm:w-4 sm:h-4 rounded-full flex-shrink-0"
02977| 						style={{ backgroundColor: personaColor }}
02978| 					/>
02979| 				) : (
02980| 					<Bot className="w-3 h-3 sm:w-4 sm:h-4 text-primary flex-shrink-0" />
02981| 				)}
02982| 				<span className="text-sm font-medium text-foreground">
02983| 					{isUser ? "You" : assistantName}
02984| 				</span>
02985| 				{group.messages.length > 1 && (
02986| 					<span
02987| 						className={cn(
02988| 							"text-[9px] sm:text-[10px] px-1 border leading-none",
02989| 							isUser
02990| 								? "border-primary/30 text-primary"
02991| 								: "border-border text-muted-foreground",
02992| 						)}
02993| 					>
02994| 						{group.messages.length}
02995| 					</span>
02996| 				)}
02997| 				<div className="flex-1" />
02998| 				{createdAt && !Number.isNaN(createdAt.getTime()) && (
02999| 					<span className="text-[9px] sm:text-[10px] text-foreground/50 dark:text-muted-foreground leading-none sm:leading-normal">
03000| 						{createdAt.toLocaleTimeString([], {
03001| 							hour: "2-digit",
03002| 							minute: "2-digit",
03003| 						})}
03004| 					</span>
03005| 				)}
03006| 				{/* Copy button - full size on desktop, compact on mobile */}
03007| 				{allTextContent && (
03008| 					<CopyButton
03009| 						text={allTextContent}
03010| 						className="hidden sm:block opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 ml-2"
03011| 					/>
03012| 				)}
03013| 				{allTextContent && (
03014| 					<CompactCopyButton text={allTextContent} className="sm:hidden ml-2" />
03015| 				)}
03016| 			</div>
03017| 
03018| 			{/* Content - render segments in order */}
03019| 			<div className="px-2 sm:px-4 py-2 sm:py-3 group space-y-3 overflow-hidden">
03020| 				{segments.length === 0 && !isUser && (
03021| 					<div className="flex items-center gap-3 text-muted-foreground text-sm">
03022| 						<KnightRiderSpinner />
03023| 						<span>Working...</span>
03024| 					</div>
03025| 				)}
03026| 				{segments.length === 0 && isUser && (
03027| 					<span className="text-muted-foreground italic text-sm">
03028| 						No content
03029| 					</span>
03030| 				)}
03031| 
03032| 				{segments.map((segment) => {
03033| 					if (segment.type === "text") {
03034| 						return (
03035| 							<div key={segment.key} className="overflow-hidden">
03036| 								<MarkdownRenderer
03037| 									content={segment.content}
03038| 									className="text-sm text-foreground leading-relaxed overflow-hidden"
03039| 								/>
03040| 							</div>
03041| 						);
03042| 					}
03043| 
03044| 					if (segment.type === "tool") {
03045| 						return (
03046| 							<ToolCallCard
03047| 								key={segment.key}
03048| 								part={segment.part}
03049| 								defaultCollapsed={true}
03050| 								hideTodoTools={true}
03051| 							/>
03052| 						);
03053| 					}
03054| 
03055| 					if (segment.type === "other") {
03056| 						return <OtherPartCard key={segment.key} part={segment.part} />;
03057| 					}
03058| 
03059| 					return null;
03060| 				})}
03061| 			</div>
03062| 		</div>
03063| 	);
03064| });

03066| const OtherPartCard = memo(function OtherPartCard({
03067| 	part,
03068| }: { part: OpenCodePart }) {
03069| 	const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
03070| 
03071| 	const getPartLabel = () => {

03073| 			case "reasoning":
03074| 				return "Reasoning";
03075| 			case "file":
03076| 				return "File";
03077| 			case "snapshot":
03078| 				return "Snapshot";
03079| 			case "patch":
03080| 				return "Patch";
03081| 			case "agent":
03082| 				return "Agent";
03083| 			case "step-start":
03084| 				return "Step Start";
03085| 			case "step-finish":
03086| 				return "Step Finish";
03087| 			case "retry":
03088| 				return "Retry";
03089| 			case "compaction":
03090| 				return "Compaction";
03091| 			case "subtask":
03092| 				return "Subtask";
03093| 			default:
03094| 				return part.type;
03095| 		}
03096| 	};
03097| 
03098| 	const content =
03099| 		part.text ||
03100| 		(part.metadata ? JSON.stringify(part.metadata, null, 2) : null);
03101| 	if (!content) return null;
03102| 
03103| 	return (

03105| 			<button

03107| 				onClick={() => setIsOpen(!isOpen)}
03108| 				className="w-full flex items-center gap-2 px-3 py-2 text-left hover:bg-muted/50 transition-colors"
03109| 			>
03110| 				<ChevronDown
03111| 					className={cn(
03112| 						"w-4 h-4 text-muted-foreground transition-transform",
03113| 						isOpen && "rotate-180",
03114| 					)}
03115| 				/>
03116| 				<span className="text-xs uppercase tracking-wide text-muted-foreground">
03117| 					{getPartLabel()}
03118| 				</span>
03119| 			</button>
03120| 
03121| 			{isOpen && (

03123| 					<pre className="text-xs text-muted-foreground mt-2 whitespace-pre-wrap overflow-x-auto">
03124| 						{content}

03127| 			)}
03128| 		</div>
03129| 	);

- Tightened the "near bottom" threshold from 150px to 100px
- Auto-scroll stays disabled until user clicks "Jump to bottom" button

### 5. Show jump-to-bottom button appropriately (`sessions/index.tsx:1417-1422`)
- Button now shows whenever content overflows the viewport AND user is more than 50px from bottom
- Previously only showed when 300px+ from bottom, now shows earlier for better UX

```
# Config

Using the OpenCode JSON config.

You can configure OpenCode using a JSON config file.

---

## [Format](#format)

OpenCode supports both **JSON** and **JSONC** (JSON with Comments) formats.

opencode.jsonc

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  // Theme configuration  "theme": "opencode",  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",  "autoupdate": true,}
```

---

## [Locations](#locations)

You can place your config in a couple of different locations and they have a different order of precedence.

Note

Configuration files are **merged together**, not replaced.

Configuration files are merged together, not replaced. Settings from the following config locations are combined. Where later configs override earlier ones only for conflicting keys. Non-conflicting settings from all configs are preserved.

For example, if your global config sets `theme: "opencode"` and `autoupdate: true`, and your project config sets `model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"`, the final configuration will include all three settings.

---

### [Global](#global)

Place your global OpenCode config in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`. You’ll want to use the global config for things like themes, providers, or keybinds.

---

### [Per project](#per-project)

You can also add a `opencode.json` in your project. Settings from this config are merged with and can override the global config. This is useful for configuring providers or modes specific to your project.

Tip

Place project specific config in the root of your project.

When OpenCode starts up, it looks for a config file in the current directory or traverse up to the nearest Git directory.

This is also safe to be checked into Git and uses the same schema as the global one.

---

### [Custom path](#custom-path)

You can also specify a custom config file path using the `OPENCODE_CONFIG` environment variable.

Terminal window

```
export OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/to/my/custom-config.jsonopencode run "Hello world"
```

Settings from this config are merged with and **can override** the global and project configs.

---

### [Custom directory](#custom-directory)

You can specify a custom config directory using the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable. This directory will be searched for agents, commands, modes, and plugins just like the standard `.opencode` directory, and should follow the same structure.

Terminal window

```
export OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR=/path/to/my/config-directoryopencode run "Hello world"
```

The custom directory is loaded after the global config and `.opencode` directories, so it **can override** their settings.

---

## [Schema](#schema)

The config file has a schema that’s defined in [**`opencode.ai/config.json`**](https://opencode.ai/config.json).

Your editor should be able to validate and autocomplete based on the schema.

---

### [TUI](#tui)

You can configure TUI-specific settings through the `tui` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "tui": {    "scroll_speed": 3,    "scroll_acceleration": {      "enabled": true    },    "diff_style": "auto"  }}
```

Available options:

-   `scroll_acceleration.enabled` - Enable macOS-style scroll acceleration. **Takes precedence over `scroll_speed`.**
-   `scroll_speed` - Custom scroll speed multiplier (default: `1`, minimum: `1`). Ignored if `scroll_acceleration.enabled` is `true`.
-   `diff_style` - Control diff rendering. `"auto"` adapts to terminal width, `"stacked"` always shows single column.

[Learn more about using the TUI here](/docs/tui).

---

### [Server](#server)

You can configure server settings for the `opencode serve` and `opencode web` commands through the `server` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "server": {    "port": 4096,    "hostname": "0.0.0.0",    "mdns": true,    "cors": ["http://localhost:5173"]  }}
```

Available options:

-   `port` - Port to listen on.
-   `hostname` - Hostname to listen on. When `mdns` is enabled and no hostname is set, defaults to `0.0.0.0`.
-   `mdns` - Enable mDNS service discovery. This allows other devices on the network to discover your OpenCode server.
-   `cors` - Additional origins to allow for CORS when using the HTTP server from a browser-based client. Values must be full origins (scheme + host + optional port), eg `https://app.example.com`.

[Learn more about the server here](/docs/server).

---

### [Tools](#tools)

You can manage the tools an LLM can use through the `tools` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "tools": {    "write": false,    "bash": false  }}
```

[Learn more about tools here](/docs/tools).

---

### [Models](#models)

You can configure the providers and models you want to use in your OpenCode config through the `provider`, `model` and `small_model` options.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "provider": {},  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",  "small_model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"}
```

The `small_model` option configures a separate model for lightweight tasks like title generation. By default, OpenCode tries to use a cheaper model if one is available from your provider, otherwise it falls back to your main model.

Provider options can include `timeout` and `setCacheKey`:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "provider": {    "anthropic": {      "options": {        "timeout": 600000,        "setCacheKey": true      }    }  }}
```

-   `timeout` - Request timeout in milliseconds (default: 300000). Set to `false` to disable.
-   `setCacheKey` - Ensure a cache key is always set for designated provider.

You can also configure [local models](/docs/models#local). [Learn more](/docs/models).

---

### [Themes](#themes)

You can configure the theme you want to use in your OpenCode config through the `theme` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "theme": ""}
```

[Learn more here](/docs/themes).

---

### [Agents](#agents)

You can configure specialized agents for specific tasks through the `agent` option.

opencode.jsonc

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "agent": {    "code-reviewer": {      "description": "Reviews code for best practices and potential issues",      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",      "prompt": "You are a code reviewer. Focus on security, performance, and maintainability.",      "tools": {        // Disable file modification tools for review-only agent        "write": false,        "edit": false,      },    },  },}
```

You can also define agents using markdown files in `~/.config/opencode/agent/` or `.opencode/agent/`. [Learn more here](/docs/agents).

---

### [Default agent](#default-agent)

You can set the default agent using the `default_agent` option. This determines which agent is used when none is explicitly specified.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "default_agent": "plan"}
```

The default agent must be a primary agent (not a subagent). This can be a built-in agent like `"build"` or `"plan"`, or a [custom agent](/docs/agents) you’ve defined. If the specified agent doesn’t exist or is a subagent, OpenCode will fall back to `"build"` with a warning.

This setting applies across all interfaces: TUI, CLI (`opencode run`), desktop app, and GitHub Action.

---

### [Sharing](#sharing)

You can configure the [share](/docs/share) feature through the `share` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "share": "manual"}
```

This takes:

-   `"manual"` - Allow manual sharing via commands (default)
-   `"auto"` - Automatically share new conversations
-   `"disabled"` - Disable sharing entirely

By default, sharing is set to manual mode where you need to explicitly share conversations using the `/share` command.

---

### [Commands](#commands)

You can configure custom commands for repetitive tasks through the `command` option.

opencode.jsonc

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "command": {    "test": {      "template": "Run the full test suite with coverage report and show any failures.\nFocus on the failing tests and suggest fixes.",      "description": "Run tests with coverage",      "agent": "build",      "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5",    },    "component": {      "template": "Create a new React component named $ARGUMENTS with TypeScript support.\nInclude proper typing and basic structure.",      "description": "Create a new component",    },  },}
```

You can also define commands using markdown files in `~/.config/opencode/command/` or `.opencode/command/`. [Learn more here](/docs/commands).

---

### [Keybinds](#keybinds)

You can customize your keybinds through the `keybinds` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "keybinds": {}}
```

[Learn more here](/docs/keybinds).

---

### [Autoupdate](#autoupdate)

OpenCode will automatically download any new updates when it starts up. You can disable this with the `autoupdate` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "autoupdate": false}
```

If you don’t want updates but want to be notified when a new version is available, set `autoupdate` to `"notify"`.

---

### [Formatters](#formatters)

You can configure code formatters through the `formatter` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "formatter": {    "prettier": {      "disabled": true    },    "custom-prettier": {      "command": ["npx", "prettier", "--write", "$FILE"],      "environment": {        "NODE_ENV": "development"      },      "extensions": [".js", ".ts", ".jsx", ".tsx"]    }  }}
```

[Learn more about formatters here](/docs/formatters).

---

### [Permissions](#permissions)

By default, opencode **allows all operations** without requiring explicit approval. You can change this using the `permission` option.

For example, to ensure that the `edit` and `bash` tools require user approval:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "permission": {    "edit": "ask",    "bash": "ask"  }}
```

[Learn more about permissions here](/docs/permissions).

---

### [Compaction](#compaction)

You can control context compaction behavior through the `compaction` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "compaction": {    "auto": true,    "prune": true  }}
```

-   `auto` - Automatically compact the session when context is full (default: `true`).
-   `prune` - Remove old tool outputs to save tokens (default: `true`).

---

### [Watcher](#watcher)

You can configure file watcher ignore patterns through the `watcher` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "watcher": {    "ignore": ["node_modules/**", "dist/**", ".git/**"]  }}
```

Patterns follow glob syntax. Use this to exclude noisy directories from file watching.

---

### [MCP servers](#mcp-servers)

You can configure MCP servers you want to use through the `mcp` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "mcp": {}}
```

[Learn more here](/docs/mcp-servers).

---

### [Plugins](#plugins)

[Plugins](/docs/plugins) extend OpenCode with custom tools, hooks, and integrations.

Place plugin files in `.opencode/plugin/` or `~/.config/opencode/plugin/`. You can also load plugins from npm through the `plugin` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "plugin": ["opencode-helicone-session", "@my-org/custom-plugin"]}
```

[Learn more here](/docs/plugins).

---

### [Instructions](#instructions)

You can configure the instructions for the model you’re using through the `instructions` option.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "instructions": ["CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guidelines.md", ".cursor/rules/*.md"]}
```

This takes an array of paths and glob patterns to instruction files. [Learn more about rules here](/docs/rules).

---

### [Disabled providers](#disabled-providers)

You can disable providers that are loaded automatically through the `disabled_providers` option. This is useful when you want to prevent certain providers from being loaded even if their credentials are available.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "disabled_providers": ["openai", "gemini"]}
```

Note

The `disabled_providers` takes priority over `enabled_providers`.

The `disabled_providers` option accepts an array of provider IDs. When a provider is disabled:

-   It won’t be loaded even if environment variables are set.
-   It won’t be loaded even if API keys are configured through the `/connect` command.
-   The provider’s models won’t appear in the model selection list.

---

### [Enabled providers](#enabled-providers)

You can specify an allowlist of providers through the `enabled_providers` option. When set, only the specified providers will be enabled and all others will be ignored.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "enabled_providers": ["anthropic", "openai"]}
```

This is useful when you want to restrict OpenCode to only use specific providers rather than disabling them one by one.

Note

The `disabled_providers` takes priority over `enabled_providers`.

If a provider appears in both `enabled_providers` and `disabled_providers`, the `disabled_providers` takes priority for backwards compatibility.

---

### [Experimental](#experimental)

The `experimental` key contains options that are under active development.

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "experimental": {}}
```

Caution

Experimental options are not stable. They may change or be removed without notice.

---

## [Variables](#variables)

You can use variable substitution in your config files to reference environment variables and file contents.

---

### [Env vars](#env-vars)

Use `{env:VARIABLE_NAME}` to substitute environment variables:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "model": "{env:OPENCODE_MODEL}",  "provider": {    "anthropic": {      "models": {},      "options": {        "apiKey": "{env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"      }    }  }}
```

If the environment variable is not set, it will be replaced with an empty string.

---

### [Files](#files)

Use `{file:path/to/file}` to substitute the contents of a file:

opencode.json

```
{  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",  "instructions": ["./custom-instructions.md"],  "provider": {    "openai": {      "options": {        "apiKey": "{file:~/.secrets/openai-key}"      }    }  }}
```

File paths can be:

-   Relative to the config file directory
-   Or absolute paths starting with `/` or `~`

These are useful for:

-   Keeping sensitive data like API keys in separate files.
-   Including large instruction files without cluttering your config.
-   Sharing common configuration snippets across multiple config files.

[Edit this page](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/edit/dev/packages/web/src/content/docs/config.mdx) [Find a bug? Open an issue](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/new) [Join our Discord community](https://opencode.ai/discord)

© [Anomaly](https://anoma.ly)

Jan 5, 2026
```

### Current Task - IN PROGRESS
**Adding Agent Settings to the right sidebar** - A UI for editing `opencode.json` local to the repo.

We fetched the OpenCode schema from `https://opencode.ai/config.json` - it's a comprehensive JSON schema with settings for:
- `model` - provider/model string
- `default_agent` - agent selection
- `share` - enum: manual/auto/disabled
- `compaction` - auto/prune booleans
- `instructions` - array of file paths
- `permission` - tool permissions (ask/allow/deny per tool)
- And many more...

### Next Steps
1. Create `AgentSettingsView` component for sidebar
2. Add API functions to read/write `opencode.json` via fileserver (expand existing `getWorkspaceConfig` in `control-plane-client.ts`)
3. Add 'settings' tab to sidebar with Settings icon
4. Implement form controls based on schema (dropdowns for enums, text inputs for strings, toggles for booleans)
5. Auto-create `opencode.json` on first setting change if it doesn't exist

### Technical Notes
- Fileserver proxy base URL pattern: `${fileserverProxyBaseUrl(sessionId)}/file?path=opencode.json`
- Existing `getWorkspaceConfig()` function reads opencode.json but has limited interface
- Need to add `saveWorkspaceConfig()` function to write back
- Schema supports JSONC (comments allowed)
- Build command: `cd frontend && bun run build`
- Dev server: `cd frontend && bun dev` (runs on localhost:5173)

```
00701| // ============================================================================
00702| // Message Format Conversion (disk format -> opencode format)
00703| // ============================================================================
00704| 
00705| import type {
00706| 	OpenCodeMessage,
00707| 	OpenCodeMessageWithParts,
00708| 	OpenCodePart,
00709| } from "./opencode-client";
00710| 
00711| /** Convert a ChatMessage (from disk) to OpenCodeMessageWithParts (for rendering) */
00712| export function convertChatMessageToOpenCode(
00713| 	msg: ChatMessage,
00714| ): OpenCodeMessageWithParts {
00715| 	// Convert parts
00716| 	const parts: OpenCodePart[] = msg.parts.map((part) => ({
00717| 		id: part.id,
00718| 		sessionID: msg.session_id,
00719| 		messageID: msg.id,
00720| 		type: part.part_type as OpenCodePart["type"],
00721| 		text: part.text ?? undefined,
00722| 		tool: part.tool_name ?? undefined,
00723| 		state: part.tool_name
00724| 			? {
00725| 					status:
00726| 						(part.tool_status as
00727| 							| "pending"
00728| 							| "running"
00729| 							| "completed"
00730| 							| "error") ?? "completed",
00731| 					input: part.tool_input as Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
00732| 					output: part.tool_output ?? undefined,
00733| 					title: part.tool_title ?? undefined,
00734| 				}
00735| 			: undefined,
00736| 	}));
00737| 
00738| 	// Build message info based on role
00739| 	const info: OpenCodeMessage =
00740| 		msg.role === "user"
00741| 			? {
00742| 					id: msg.id,
00743| 					sessionID: msg.session_id,
00744| 					role: "user" as const,
00745| 					time: { created: msg.created_at },
00746| 					agent: msg.agent ?? undefined,
00747| 					model:
00748| 						msg.provider_id && msg.model_id
00749| 							? {
00750| 									providerID: msg.provider_id,
00751| 									modelID: msg.model_id,
00752| 								}
00753| 							: undefined,
00754| 				}
00755| 			: {
00756| 					id: msg.id,
00757| 					sessionID: msg.session_id,
00758| 					role: "assistant" as const,
00759| 					time: {
00760| 						created: msg.created_at,
00761| 						completed: msg.completed_at ?? undefined,
00762| 					},
00763| 					parentID: msg.parent_id ?? "",
00764| 					modelID: msg.model_id ?? "",
00765| 					providerID: msg.provider_id ?? "",
00766| 					cost: msg.cost ?? undefined,
00767| 					tokens:
00768| 						msg.tokens_input != null || msg.tokens_output != null
00769| 							? {
00770| 									input: msg.tokens_input ?? 0,
00771| 									output: msg.tokens_output ?? 0,
00772| 									reasoning: 0,
00773| 									cache: { read: 0, write: 0 },
00774| 								}
00775| 							: undefined,
00776| 				};
00777| 
00778| 	return { info, parts };
00779| }
00780| 
00781| /** Convert an array of ChatMessages to OpenCodeMessageWithParts */
00782| export function convertChatMessagesToOpenCode(
00783| 	messages: ChatMessage[],
00784| ): OpenCodeMessageWithParts[] {
00785| 	return messages.map(convertChatMessageToOpenCode);
00786| }
```

```
00064| export function SettingsEditor({
00065| 	app,
00066| 	title,
00067| 	isAdmin = false,
00068| }: SettingsEditorProps) {
00069| 	const [schema, setSchema] = useState<Schema | null>(null);
00070| 	const [values, setValues] = useState<SettingsValues>({});
00071| 	const [pendingChanges, setPendingChanges] = useState<Record<string, unknown>>(
00072| 		{},
00073| 	);
00074| 	const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
00075| 	const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false);
00076| 	const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
00077| 	const [success, setSuccess] = useState(false);
00078| 	const [expandedSections, setExpandedSections] = useState<Set<string>>(
00079| 		new Set(),
00080| 	);
00081| 
00082| 	// Load schema and values
00083| 	const loadSettings = useCallback(async () => {
00084| 		setLoading(true);
00085| 		setError(null);
00086| 		try {
00087| 			const [schemaData, valuesData] = await Promise.all([
00088| 				getSettingsSchema(app),
00089| 				getSettingsValues(app),
00090| 			]);
00091| 			setSchema(schemaData as Schema);
00092| 			setValues(valuesData);
00093| 			setPendingChanges({});
00094| 		} catch (err) {
00095| 			setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Failed to load settings");
00096| 		} finally {
00097| 			setLoading(false);
00098| 		}
00099| 	}, [app]);
00100| 
00101| 	useEffect(() => {
00102| 		loadSettings();
00103| 	}, [loadSettings]);
00104| 
00105| 	// Save changes
00106| 	const handleSave = useCallback(async () => {
00107| 		if (Object.keys(pendingChanges).length === 0) return;
00108| 
00109| 		setSaving(true);
00110| 		setError(null);
00111| 		setSuccess(false);
00112| 		try {
00113| 			const newValues = await updateSettingsValues(app, {
00114| 				values: pendingChanges,
00115| 			});
00116| 			setValues(newValues);
00117| 			setPendingChanges({});
00118| 			setSuccess(true);
00119| 			setTimeout(() => setSuccess(false), 2000);
00120| 		} catch (err) {
00121| 			setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Failed to save settings");
00122| 		} finally {
00123| 			setSaving(false);
00124| 		}
00125| 	}, [app, pendingChanges]);
00126| 
00127| 	// Reload from disk (admin only)
00128| 	const handleReload = useCallback(async () => {
00129| 		setError(null);
00130| 		try {
00131| 			await reloadSettings(app);
00132| 			await loadSettings();
00133| 		} catch (err) {
00134| 			setError(
00135| 				err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Failed to reload settings",
00136| 			);
00137| 		}
00138| 	}, [app, loadSettings]);
00139| 
00140| 	// Update a value
00141| 	const handleValueChange = useCallback((path: string, value: unknown) => {
00142| 		setPendingChanges((prev) => ({ ...prev, [path]: value }));
00143| 	}, []);
00144| 
00145| 	// Reset a value to default
00146| 	const handleReset = useCallback(
00147| 		(path: string) => {
00148| 			const setting = values[path];
00149| 			if (setting?.default !== undefined) {
00150| 				setPendingChanges((prev) => ({ ...prev, [path]: setting.default }));
00151| 			}
00152| 		},
00153| 		[values],
00154| 	);
00155| 
00156| 	// Get effective value (pending change or current)
00157| 	const getEffectiveValue = useCallback(
00158| 		(path: string): unknown => {
00159| 			if (path in pendingChanges) return pendingChanges[path];
00160| 			return values[path]?.value;
00161| 		},
00162| 		[pendingChanges, values],
00163| 	);
00164| 
00165| 	// Check if value has been modified
00166| 	const isModified = useCallback(
00167| 		(path: string): boolean => {
00168| 			return path in pendingChanges;
00169| 		},
00170| 		[pendingChanges],
00171| 	);
00172| 
00173| 	// Toggle section expansion
00174| 	const toggleSection = useCallback((section: string) => {
00175| 		setExpandedSections((prev) => {
00176| 			const next = new Set(prev);
00177| 			if (next.has(section)) {
00178| 				next.delete(section);
00179| 			} else {
00180| 				next.add(section);
00181| 			}
00182| 			return next;
00183| 		});
00184| 	}, []);
00185| 
00186| 	if (loading) {
00187| 		return (
00188| 			<div className="flex items-center justify-center p-8">
00189| 				<Loader2 className="h-6 w-6 animate-spin text-muted-foreground" />
00190| 			</div>
00191| 		);
00192| 	}
00193| 
00194| 	if (!schema) {
00195| 		return (
00196| 			<div className="p-4 text-center text-muted-foreground">
00197| 				No settings available for {app}
00198| 			</div>
00199| 		);
00200| 	}
00201| 
00202| 	// Group properties by x-category
00203| 	const groupedProperties = groupByCategory(schema.properties || {});
00204| 	const hasChanges = Object.keys(pendingChanges).length > 0;
00205| 
00206| 	return (
00207| 		<div className="space-y-4 sm:space-y-6">
00208| 			{/* Header */}
00209| 			<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between">
00210| 				<div className="min-w-0">
00211| 					<h2 className="text-base sm:text-lg font-semibold truncate">
00212| 						{title || schema.title || `${app} Settings`}
00213| 					</h2>
00214| 					{schema.description && (

00216| 							{schema.description}
00217| 						</p>
00218| 					)}
00219| 				</div>
00220| 				<div className="flex items-center gap-2 flex-shrink-0">
00221| 					{isAdmin && (
00222| 						<Button
00223| 							type="button"
00224| 							variant="outline"

00228| 						>
00229| 							<RotateCcw className="h-4 w-4 sm:mr-1" />
00230| 							<span className="hidden sm:inline">Reload</span>
00231| 						</Button>

00233| 					<Button

00239| 					>
00240| 						{saving ? (
00241| 							<Loader2 className="h-4 w-4 sm:mr-1 animate-spin" />
00242| 						) : success ? (
00243| 							<Check className="h-4 w-4 sm:mr-1" />
00244| 						) : (
00245| 							<Save className="h-4 w-4 sm:mr-1" />
00246| 						)}
00247| 						<span className="hidden sm:inline">
00248| 							{saving ? "Saving..." : success ? "Saved" : "Save Changes"}

00252| 						</span>
00253| 					</Button>
00254| 				</div>
00255| 			</div>
00256| 
00257| 			{/* Error message */}
00258| 			{error && (
00259| 				<div className="flex items-center gap-2 p-3 bg-destructive/10 text-destructive rounded-md">
00260| 					<AlertCircle className="h-4 w-4" />
00261| 					<span className="text-sm">{error}</span>
00262| 				</div>
00263| 			)}
00264| 
00265| 			{/* Settings sections */}
00266| 			<div className="space-y-3 sm:space-y-4">
00267| 				{Object.entries(groupedProperties).map(([category, properties]) => (
00268| 					<SettingsSection
00269| 						key={category}
00270| 						category={category}
00271| 						properties={properties}
00272| 						values={values}
00273| 						getEffectiveValue={getEffectiveValue}
00274| 						isModified={isModified}
00275| 						onValueChange={handleValueChange}
00276| 						onReset={handleReset}

00278| 						onToggle={() => toggleSection(category)}
00279| 					/>
00280| 				))}
00281| 			</div>
00282| 		</div>
00283| 	);
00284| }

00286| // Group properties by x-category
00287| function groupByCategory(
00288| 	properties: Record<string, SchemaProperty>,
00289| ): Record<string, Record<string, SchemaProperty>> {
00290| 	const groups: Record<string, Record<string, SchemaProperty>> = {};
00291| 
00292| 	for (const [key, prop] of Object.entries(properties)) {
00293| 		const category = prop["x-category"] || "General";
00294| 		if (!groups[category]) groups[category] = {};
00295| 		groups[category][key] = prop;
00296| 	}
00297| 
00298| 	return groups;
00299| }
```

## Message 206: Assistant
**Timestamp:** 07:50:49

I've completed implementing the Agent Settings sidebar feature. Here's a summary of what was done:

## Summary of Changes

### 1. `frontend/lib/control-plane-client.ts`
- Expanded `WorkspaceConfig` interface with full OpenCode config fields:
  - `model` - provider/model string
  - `default_agent` - agent selection
  - `share` - sharing mode (manual/auto/disabled)
  - `compaction` - auto/prune settings
  - `instructions` - file paths array
  - `permission` - tool permissions
  - `disabled_tools`, `mcp`, `providers`
- Added `saveWorkspaceConfig()` function to write `opencode.json` via fileserver

### 2. `frontend/apps/sessions/AgentSettingsView.tsx` (new file)
- Created new component for editing workspace settings
- Features:
  - Model input field
  - Default agent dropdown (populated from OpenCode agents API)
  - Share mode dropdown
  - Compaction toggles (auto/prune)
  - Instructions textarea (multi-line)
  - Raw JSON view (expandable)
  - Save/reload functionality with pending changes tracking
  - Visual indicators for modified fields

### 3. `frontend/apps/sessions/index.tsx`
- Added `Settings` icon import from lucide-react
- Added `"settings"` to `ActiveView` type
- Added lazy import for `AgentSettingsView`
- Added Settings tab button in both mobile and desktop layouts
- Added Settings view rendering in both layouts

The Settings tab now appears in the right sidebar (desktop) or tab bar (mobile) with a gear icon. Users can edit their workspace's `opencode.json` configuration directly from the UI.

**Timestamp:** 07:56:43

Both compile. Now you'll need to restart the fileserver for the new PUT endpoint to be available. The fileserver now supports:

- `GET /file?path=...` - Read file
- `POST /file?path=...` - Upload file (multipart)
- `PUT /file?path=...` - Write file contents directly (for simple text/JSON)
- `DELETE /file?path=...` - Delete file

After restarting the fileserver, the Settings tab should be able to save `opencode.json`.

```
              }
```
```
            },

            },

              "description": "Description of when to use the agent",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "mode": {
              "type": "string",
              "enum": [
                "subagent",
                "primary",
                "all"
              ]
            },
            "options": {
              "type": "object",
              "propertyNames": {
                "type": "string"
              },
              "additionalProperties": {}
            },
            "color": {
              "description": "Hex color code for the agent (e.g., #FF5733)",
              "type": "string",
              "pattern": "^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$"
            },
            "steps": {
              "description": "Maximum number of agentic iterations before forcing text-only response",
              "type": "integer",
              "exclusiveMinimum": 0,
              "maximum": 9007199254740991
            },

            "permission": {

                {
                  "type": "object",
                  "properties": {

                      "ref": "PermissionRuleConfig",
                      "anyOf": [

                          "ref": "PermissionActionConfig",
                          "type": "string",
                          "enum": [
                            "ask",
                            "allow",
                            "deny"
                          ]
                        },
                        {
                          "ref": "PermissionObjectConfig",
                          "type": "object",
                          "propertyNames": {
                            "type": "string"
                          },

                            "type": "string",
                            "enum": [
                              "ask",
                              "allow",
                              "deny"
                            ]
                          }
                        }
                      ]
                    },
                    "edit": {
                      "ref": "PermissionRuleConfig",
                      "anyOf": [
                        {
                          "ref": "PermissionActionConfig",
                          "type": "string",
                          "enum": [
                            "ask",
                            "allow",
                            "deny"

                        },
```

### Project Overview
We're working on **Octo**, a frontend React/TypeScript application that provides a web UI for OpenCode (an AI coding assistant). The frontend communicates with a control-plane backend and a fileserver for file operations.

### What We Completed

#### 1. Agent Settings Sidebar Feature
We added a new "Settings" tab to the right sidebar that allows users to edit `opencode.json` configuration for their workspace.

**Files created/modified:**

1. **`/home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/frontend/apps/sessions/AgentSettingsView.tsx`** (NEW)
   - Component for editing workspace settings
   - Fetches config from fileserver via `getWorkspaceConfig()`
   - Fetches available agents from OpenCode API via `fetchAgents(opencodeBaseUrl)`
   - Settings include: Model, Default Agent, Share Mode, Compaction (auto/prune), Instructions
   - Shows raw JSON view in expandable section
   - Has save/reload functionality with pending changes tracking

2. **`/home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/frontend/lib/control-plane-client.ts`**
   - Expanded `WorkspaceConfig` interface with full OpenCode config fields
   - Added `saveWorkspaceConfig()` function using PUT request

3. **`/home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/frontend/apps/sessions/index.tsx`**
   - Added `Settings` icon import from lucide-react
   - Added `"settings"` to `ActiveView` type
   - Added lazy import for `AgentSettingsView`
   - Added Settings tab button in both mobile and desktop sidebar layouts
   - Added Settings view rendering

4. **`/home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/fileserver/src/handlers.rs`**
   - Added `write_file()` handler for PUT `/file` endpoint
   - Allows direct file content writes (simpler than multipart POST)

5. **`/home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/fileserver/src/routes.rs`**
   - Added `.route("/file", put(handlers::write_file))` route

### Current Issue We Just Fixed
The Default Agent dropdown was only showing "Default" because `fetchAgents()` requires `opencodeBaseUrl` (the OpenCode API base URL), not the `sessionId`. We just fixed this by:
- Getting `opencodeBaseUrl` from `useApp()` context
- Passing it to `fetchAgents(opencodeBaseUrl)` instead of `fetchAgents(sessionId)`

### What Needs Testing
1. Verify the Settings tab loads agents correctly from the running OpenCode instance
2. Test saving configuration to `opencode.json`
3. The fileserver needs to be rebuilt and restarted for the new PUT endpoint

### Build Commands
```bash
# Build fileserver (needs restart after)
cd /home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/fileserver && cargo build

# Build frontend
cd /home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/frontend && bun run build

# Dev server
cd /home/wismut/byteowlz/octo/frontend && bun dev
```

### OpenCode Config Schema Reference
Key settings from `https://opencode.ai/config.json`:
- `model` - Provider/model string (e.g., "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514")
- `default_agent` - Which agent to use (build, plan, explore, general, etc.)
- `share` - Session sharing mode: "manual" | "auto" | "disabled"
- `compaction` - `{ auto?: boolean, prune?: boolean }`
- `instructions` - Array of instruction file paths
- `permission` - Tool permissions (ask/allow/deny per tool)
- `provider` - Custom provider configurations
- `mcp` - MCP server configurations

### Potential Next Steps
1. Test the agent dropdown now that it uses `opencodeBaseUrl`
2. Add more settings from the OpenCode schema (permissions, provider config, etc.)
3. Add validation for model string format
4. Consider adding a "Reset to defaults" button
5. Add visual feedback when config file doesn't exist vs. is empty

### Key Architecture Notes
- `useApp()` provides: `selectedWorkspaceSession`, `opencodeBaseUrl`, and other context
- `sessionId` is used for fileserver routes: `fileserverProxyBaseUrl(sessionId)/file?path=opencode.json`
- `opencodeBaseUrl` is used for OpenCode API calls like `fetchAgents()`
- Radix UI Select doesn't allow empty string values - use sentinel like `"__none__"` instead

```
00122| type ApiErrorResponse = {
00123| 	error?: string;
00124| };
00125| 
00126| const trimTrailingSlash = (value: string) => value.replace(/\/$/, "");
00127| const controlPlaneStorageKey = "octo:controlPlaneUrl";
00128| 
00129| const env =
00130| 	(import.meta as ImportMeta & { env?: Record<string, string | undefined> })
00131| 		.env ?? (typeof process !== "undefined" ? process.env : {});
00132| 
00133| function normalizeControlPlaneUrl(value: string | null | undefined): string {
00134| 	if (!value) return "";
00135| 	return trimTrailingSlash(value.trim());
00136| }
00137| 
00138| export function getControlPlaneBaseUrl(): string {
00139| 	if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
00140| 		try {
00141| 			const stored = window.localStorage.getItem(controlPlaneStorageKey);
00142| 			const normalized = normalizeControlPlaneUrl(stored);
00143| 			if (normalized) return normalized;
00144| 		} catch (err) {
00145| 			console.warn("[control-plane] Failed to read stored base URL:", err);
00146| 		}
00147| 	}
00148| 	return normalizeControlPlaneUrl(env.VITE_CONTROL_PLANE_URL ?? "");
00149| }
00150| 
00151| export function setControlPlaneBaseUrl(value: string | null): void {
00152| 	if (typeof window === "undefined") return;
00153| 	const normalized = normalizeControlPlaneUrl(value ?? "");
00154| 	try {
00155| 		if (normalized) {
00156| 			window.localStorage.setItem(controlPlaneStorageKey, normalized);
00157| 		} else {
00158| 			window.localStorage.removeItem(controlPlaneStorageKey);
00159| 		}
00160| 	} catch (err) {
00161| 		console.warn("[control-plane] Failed to store base URL:", err);
00162| 	}
00163| }
00164| 
00165| export function controlPlaneDirectBaseUrl(): string {
00166| 	return getControlPlaneBaseUrl();
00167| }
00168| 
00169| export function controlPlaneApiUrl(path: string): string {
00170| 	const base = getControlPlaneBaseUrl();
00171| 	const normalizedPath = path.startsWith("/") ? path : `/${path}`;
00172| 	if (base) {
00173| 		const stripped = normalizedPath.startsWith("/api")
00174| 			? normalizedPath.replace(/^\/api/, "")
00175| 			: normalizedPath;
00176| 		return `${base}${stripped}`;
00177| 	}
00178| 	if (normalizedPath.startsWith("/api")) return normalizedPath;
00179| 	return `/api${normalizedPath}`;
00180| }
00181| 
00182| async function readApiError(res: Response): Promise<string> {
00183| 	const contentType = res.headers.get("content-type") ?? "";
00184| 	if (contentType.includes("application/json")) {
00185| 		const parsed = (await res
00186| 			.json()
00187| 			.catch(() => null)) as ApiErrorResponse | null;
00188| 		if (parsed?.error) return parsed.error;
00189| 	}
00190| 	return (await res.text().catch(() => res.statusText)) || res.statusText;
00191| }

00707| 	OpenCodeMessageWithParts,
00708| 	OpenCodePart,
00709| } from "./opencode-client";
00710| 
00711| /** Convert a ChatMessage (from disk) to OpenCodeMessageWithParts (for rendering) */
00712| export function convertChatMessageToOpenCode(
00713| 	msg: ChatMessage,
00714| ): OpenCodeMessageWithParts {
00715| 	// Convert parts
00716| 	const parts: OpenCodePart[] = msg.parts.map((part) => ({
00717| 		id: part.id,
00718| 		sessionID: msg.session_id,
00719| 		messageID: msg.id,
00720| 		type: part.part_type as OpenCodePart["type"],
00721| 		text: part.text ?? undefined,
00722| 		tool: part.tool_name ?? undefined,
00723| 		state: part.tool_name
00724| 			? {
00725| 					status:
00726| 						(part.tool_status as
00727| 							| "pending"
00728| 							| "running"
00729| 							| "completed"
00730| 							| "error") ?? "completed",
00731| 					input: part.tool_input as Record<string, unknown> | undefined,
00732| 					output: part.tool_output ?? undefined,
00733| 					title: part.tool_title ?? undefined,
00734| 				}
00735| 			: undefined,
00736| 	}));
00737| 
00738| 	// Build message info based on role
00739| 	const info: OpenCodeMessage =
00740| 		msg.role === "user"
00741| 			? {
00742| 					id: msg.id,
00743| 					sessionID: msg.session_id,
00744| 					role: "user" as const,
00745| 					time: { created: msg.created_at },
00746| 					agent: msg.agent ?? undefined,
00747| 					model:
00748| 						msg.provider_id && msg.model_id
00749| 							? {
00750| 									providerID: msg.provider_id,
00751| 									modelID: msg.model_id,
00752| 								}
00753| 							: undefined,
00754| 				}
00755| 			: {
00756| 					id: msg.id,
00757| 					sessionID: msg.session_id,
00758| 					role: "assistant" as const,
00759| 					time: {
00760| 						created: msg.created_at,
00761| 						completed: msg.completed_at ?? undefined,
00762| 					},
00763| 					parentID: msg.parent_id ?? "",
00764| 					modelID: msg.model_id ?? "",
00765| 					providerID: msg.provider_id ?? "",
00766| 					cost: msg.cost ?? undefined,
00767| 					tokens:
00768| 						msg.tokens_input != null || msg.tokens_output != null
00769| 							? {
00770| 									input: msg.tokens_input ?? 0,
00771| 									output: msg.tokens_output ?? 0,
00772| 									reasoning: 0,
00773| 									cache: { read: 0, write: 0 },
00774| 								}
00775| 							: undefined,
00776| 				};
00777| 
00778| 	return { info, parts };
00779| }
00780| 
00781| /** Convert an array of ChatMessages to OpenCodeMessageWithParts */
00782| export function convertChatMessagesToOpenCode(
00783| 	messages: ChatMessage[],
00784| ): OpenCodeMessageWithParts[] {
00785| 	return messages.map(convertChatMessageToOpenCode);
00786| }
```

Now I understand the permission schema. The `permission` field can be:
1. A global action: `"ask"` | `"allow"` | `"deny"`
2. Or an object with tool-specific permissions, where each tool can have either:
   - A simple action: `"ask"` | `"allow"` | `"deny"`
   - Or an object with pattern-specific rules

The main tools are: `read`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `list`, `bash`, `task`, `external_directory`, `todowrite`, `todoread`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `codesearch`, `lsp`, `doom_loop`

## Message 261: Assistant

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of the changes:

## Summary

### Changes made:

1. **Removed redundant Settings icon** from `AgentSettingsView.tsx` header (it was duplicative since the tab already shows the icon)

2. **Updated `control-plane-client.ts`** - Enhanced the permission types:
   - Added `PermissionAction` type: `"ask" | "allow" | "deny"`
   - Added `PermissionRule` type that can be either a simple action or pattern-specific rules
   - Updated `PermissionConfig` to support both global actions and per-tool configurations

3. **Added Permissions section** to `AgentSettingsView.tsx`:
   - Lists 14 known OpenCode tools (read, edit, bash, glob, grep, list, task, webfetch, websearch, codesearch, todowrite, todoread, lsp, external_directory)
   - Supports two modes:
     - **Global permission**: Set `allow`, `ask`, or `deny` for ALL tools at once
     - **Per-tool permissions**: Configure each tool individually when "Per-tool" is selected
   - Shows tool name and description for each tool
   - Scrollable list with max height for the per-tool section
   - Shows "modified" badge when permissions have been changed
   - Integrates with the existing save/reload flow

### UI Structure:
- **All Tools** dropdown at the top to set global permission or switch to per-tool mode
- When in per-tool mode, each tool shows:
  - Tool label and description
  - Dropdown with: Default, Allow, Ask, Deny options

```
00161| /// Sanitize a filename by removing dangerous characters and path components.
00162| /// Returns None if the filename is invalid or empty after sanitization.
00163| fn sanitize_filename(filename: &str) -> Option<String> {
00164|     // Reject empty filenames
00165|     if filename.is_empty() {
00166|         return None;
00167|     }
00168| 
00169|     // Remove null bytes and other control characters
00170|     let sanitized: String = filename
00171|         .chars()
00172|         .filter(|c| !c.is_control() && *c != '\0')
00173|         .collect();
00174| 
00175|     // Remove path separators and dangerous characters
00176|     let sanitized: String = sanitized
00177|         .chars()
00178|         .map(|c| match c {
00179|             '/' | '\\' | ':' | '*' | '?' | '"' | '<' | '>' | '|' => '_',
00180|             _ => c,
00181|         })
00182|         .collect();
00183| 
00184|     // Remove leading/trailing dots and spaces (Windows compatibility + security)
00185|     let sanitized = sanitized.trim_matches(|c| c == '.' || c == ' ');
00186| 
00187|     // Reject if empty after sanitization
00188|     if sanitized.is_empty() {
00189|         return None;
00190|     }
00191| 
00192|     // Reject reserved Windows names (for cross-platform safety)
00193|     let upper = sanitized.to_uppercase();
00194|     let reserved = [
00195|         "CON", "PRN", "AUX", "NUL", "COM1", "COM2", "COM3", "COM4", "COM5", "COM6", "COM7", "COM8",
00196|         "COM9", "LPT1", "LPT2", "LPT3", "LPT4", "LPT5", "LPT6", "LPT7", "LPT8", "LPT9",
00197|     ];
00198|     if reserved
00199|         .iter()
00200|         .any(|r| upper == *r || upper.starts_with(&format!("{}.", r)))
00201|     {
00202|         return None;
00203|     }
00204| 
00205|     // Limit filename length
00206|     if sanitized.len() > 255 {
00207|         return Some(sanitized[..255].to_string());
00208|     }
00209| 
00210|     Some(sanitized.to_string())
00211| }
00212| 
00213| /// Resolve and validate a path, ensuring it's within the root directory.
00214| ///
00215| /// This function is designed to prevent path traversal attacks by:
00216| /// 1. Building the path component-by-component, rejecting any parent directory (..) references
00217| /// 2. Validating the final path is within the root directory
00218| /// 3. Using a deterministic path building approach that doesn't rely on filesystem state
00219| ///
00220| /// Note: For existing paths, the caller should canonicalize and re-verify after this check
00221| /// to handle symbolic link attacks (TOCTOU mitigation).
00222| fn resolve_path(root: &Path, relative: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, FileServerError> {
00223|     // Normalize and split the relative path
00224|     let relative = relative.trim_start_matches('/');
00225| 
00226|     // Handle empty path or "."
00227|     if relative.is_empty() || relative == "." {
00228|         return Ok(root.to_path_buf());
00229|     }
00230| 
00231|     // Build the path component-by-component, rejecting traversal attempts
00232|     let mut result = root.to_path_buf();
00233| 
00234|     for component in Path::new(relative).components() {
00235|         match component {
00236|             Component::Normal(name) => {
00237|                 // Check for embedded null bytes or other dangerous characters in the name
00238|                 let name_str = name.to_string_lossy();
00239|                 if name_str.contains('\0') {
00240|                     warn!("Path component contains null byte: {:?}", name);
00241|                     return Err(FileServerError::PathTraversal);
00242|                 }
00243|                 result.push(name);
00244|             }
00245|             Component::ParentDir => {
00246|                 // ALWAYS reject parent directory references - this is the key security fix
00247|                 // Even if they would resolve to within root, they indicate malicious intent
00248|                 warn!("Path traversal attempt detected: parent directory (..) in path");
00249|                 return Err(FileServerError::PathTraversal);
00250|             }
00251|             Component::CurDir => {
00252|                 // Current directory (.) is safe, just skip it
00253|                 continue;
00254|             }
00255|             Component::RootDir | Component::Prefix(_) => {
00256|                 // Absolute path components are not allowed
00257|                 warn!("Absolute path component in relative path");
00258|                 return Err(FileServerError::PathTraversal);
00259|             }
00260|         }
00261|     }
00262| 
00263|     // Final validation: ensure the built path starts with root
00264|     // This is a belt-and-suspenders check
00265|     if !result.starts_with(root) {
00266|         error!(
00267|             "Path resolution resulted in path outside root: {:?}",
00268|             result
00269|         );
00270|         return Err(FileServerError::PathTraversal);
00271|     }
00272| 
00273|     Ok(result)
00274| }
00275| 
00276| /// Safely resolve a path and validate it exists within root.
00277| /// This function handles both path building and symlink resolution safely.
00278| ///
00279| /// For operations that need to access the filesystem, use this function
00280| /// to get a canonical path that is guaranteed to be within root.
00281| fn resolve_and_verify_path(root: &Path, relative: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, FileServerError> {
00282|     // First, build the path without following symlinks
00283|     let built_path = resolve_path(root, relative)?;
00284| 
00285|     // If the path exists, canonicalize it and verify it's still within root
00286|     if built_path.exists() {
00287|         let canonical_root = root.canonicalize().map_err(FileServerError::Io)?;
00288|         let canonical_path = built_path.canonicalize().map_err(FileServerError::Io)?;
00289| 
00290|         // Verify the canonical path is within the canonical root
00291|         if !canonical_path.starts_with(&canonical_root) {
00292|             warn!(
00293|                 "Symlink escape attempt: {:?} resolved to {:?} which is outside {:?}",
00294|                 built_path, canonical_path, canonical_root
00295|             );
00296|             return Err(FileServerError::PathTraversal);
00297|         }
00298| 
00299|         Ok(canonical_path)
00300|     } else {
00301|         // Path doesn't exist yet - verify the parent directory
00302|         if let Some(parent) = built_path.parent() {
00303|             if parent.exists() {
00304|                 let canonical_root = root.canonicalize().map_err(FileServerError::Io)?;
00305|                 let canonical_parent = parent.canonicalize().map_err(FileServerError::Io)?;
00306| 
00307|                 if !canonical_parent.starts_with(&canonical_root) {
00308|                     warn!(
00309|                         "Parent directory escape: {:?} parent resolved outside root",
00310|                         built_path
00311|                     );
00312|                     return Err(FileServerError::PathTraversal);
00313|                 }
00314|             }
00315|         }
00316| 
00317|         Ok(built_path)
00318|     }
00319| }
00320| 
00321| /// Get relative path from root
00322| fn get_relative_path(root: &Path, full_path: &Path) -> String {
00323|     full_path
00324|         .strip_prefix(root)
00325|         .map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().to_string())
00326|         .unwrap_or_default()
00327| }
00328| 
00329| fn normalize_extension(ext: &str) -> Option<String> {
00330|     let trimmed = ext.trim();
00331|     if trimmed.is_empty() {
00332|         return None;
00333|     }
00334| 
00335|     let trimmed = trimmed.trim_start_matches('.');
00336|     if trimmed.is_empty() {
00337|         return None;
00338|     }
00339| 
00340|     Some(trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase())
00341| }
00342| 
00343| fn parse_extension_filter(ext: &Option<String>) -> Option<HashSet<String>> {
00344|     let ext = ext.as_ref()?;
00345|     let mut set = HashSet::new();
00346| 
00347|     for item in ext.split(',') {
00348|         if let Some(normalized) = normalize_extension(item) {
00349|             set.insert(normalized);
00350|         }
00351|     }
00352| 
00353|     if set.is_empty() {
00354|         None
00355|     } else {
00356|         Some(set)
00357|     }
00358| }
00359| 
00360| fn event_label(kind: &EventKind, is_dir: bool) -> Option<&'static str> {
00361|     match kind {
00362|         EventKind::Create(_) => {
00363|             if is_dir {
00364|                 Some("dir_created")
00365|             } else {
00366|                 Some("file_created")
00367|             }
00368|         }
00369|         EventKind::Modify(_) => {
00370|             if is_dir {
00371|                 None
00372|             } else {
00373|                 Some("file_modified")
00374|             }
00375|         }
00376|         EventKind::Remove(_) => {
00377|             if is_dir {
00378|                 Some("dir_deleted")
00379|             } else {
00380|                 Some("file_deleted")
00381|             }
00382|         }
00383|         _ => None,
00384|     }
00385| }

00399| const WATCH_DEBOUNCE: Duration = Duration::from_millis(250);
00400| 
00401| #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
00402| struct WatchEvent {
00403|     #[serde(rename = "type")]
00404|     event_type: &'static str,
00405|     path: String,
00406|     entry_type: &'static str,
```
